samples.summary: DOCX export still interpolates `style.alignment` into a `w:val` attribute unescaped — the same XML-attribute-injection class this delta just closed for colors
samples.evidence: `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` emits `<w:jc w:val="${align}"/>` (packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:106-109) with `align` taken verbatim from `BlockStyle.alignment`. That field is NOT a validated union at runtime: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:222` does `partial.alignment = attrs.alignment as BlockStyle['alignment']` — a raw, unchecked cast of a Yorkie tree attribute, and `normalizeBlockStyle` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:324) is just a spread over defaults, so it validates nothing. Attack: a collaborating peer (or anyone able to write the shared Yorkie doc / a crafted persisted document) sets the block attribute `alignment` to e.g. `center"/><w:r><w:fldChar w:fldCharType="begin"/></w:r><w:jc w:val="left`. When a victim exports that document to .docx, the injected markup lands verbatim in `word/document.xml`, letting the attacker synthesize arbitrary WordprocessingML (field codes, style refs, added runs) in a file the victim believes they authored. This is exactly the vector the delta cites in its own comments ("a peer's Yorkie attribute … never validated") when adding `escapeXmlAttr` to colors two lines below, so the fix is incomplete in the function it touches. Same file/function, one branch left unescaped.

samples.summary: Colors are escaped rather than validated, so hostile/garbage color strings still reach ST_HexColor attributes; the PDF path allowlists instead
samples.evidence: `escapeXmlAttr(colorHex.replace('#',''))` (docx-style-map.ts:78, :83) and `escapeXmlAttr(cell.style.backgroundColor.replace('#',''))` (docx-exporter.ts:312) keep the XML well-formed but still write arbitrary attacker-supplied text (e.g. `"/><w:b/>`) into `w:color/@w:val` and `w:shd/@w:fill`, which OOXML types as ST_HexColor. The equivalent PDF path validates with `/^#?([0-9a-f]{6})$/i` and falls back to black (packages/docs/src/export/pdf-style-map.ts:146). An allowlist here (drop the property when it is not 6-hex/`auto`) removes the whole class instead of relying on the escaper staying correct, and avoids emitting schema-invalid documents Word will offer to 'repair'. Note the color strings are attacker-reachable with no collaborator access at all: pasted HTML is read straight into styles at packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:153-154 and :416-417.

samples.summary: No test covers the newly added escaping of the table-cell `<w:shd w:fill>` value, so a regression there would be silent
samples.evidence: The delta added `escapeXmlAttr` at docx-exporter.ts:312 for cell backgrounds, but the only new security test is in packages/docs/test/export/docx-style-map.test.ts:60 and exercises `buildRunPropertiesXml` (inline runs) only. Grepping the whole packages/docs/test/export tree for `w:shd`, `escape` and `backgroundColor` finds no docx-exporter test asserting a hostile cell background is escaped, so reverting line 312 would leave the suite green while re-opening the injection.

samples.summary: Run text escaping does not strip XML-illegal control characters, so attacker-supplied text can produce an unopenable document.xml
samples.evidence: `inlineToXml` escapes only `&`, `<`, `>` (docx-exporter.ts:218-221). Characters in U+0000–U+0008/U+000B/U+000C/U+000E–U+001F are illegal in XML 1.0 content and cannot be represented by numeric references either; a peer or a pasted payload containing e.g. U+0000 in `inline.text` (paste path: packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts) yields a `word/document.xml` that Word/consumers reject outright. Impact is corruption/denial of export rather than injection, and the PDF path already strips these (packages/docs/src/export/pdf-style-map.ts:71) — the DOCX path should do the same.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end in the repo. The sink is present verbatim: docx-style-map.ts:106-109 interpolates `align` into `<w:jc w:val="${align}"/>` with no escapeXmlAttr, even though the same file escapes fontFamily (:54-57), color (:78) and backgroundColor (:83) using the helper defined at :26-33. The `align !== 'left'` test only excludes the literal string 'left', so hostile values pass through. The value reaches the sink unmodified: docx-exporter.ts:182-183 passes block.style directly, and the returned string is embedded raw into the paragraph XML at :187 (word/document.xml). The taint source is unvalidated at runtime: yorkie-doc-store.ts:222 does a bare `attrs.alignment as BlockStyle['alignment']` cast of a peer-writable Yorkie tree attribute, the union at model/types.ts:103 is compile-time only, and normalizeBlockStyle (model/types.ts:324-326) is a plain spread over defaults that rejects nothing. I searched for a guard that could make this unreachable and found only the DOCX importer (import/docx-style-map.ts:104-107), which maps to a closed set with an else->'left' fallback but covers only the import path, not the Yorkie collaboration path, so it does not close this vector. This is XML/template injection via unsafe input handling, in the Security lane: a collaborating peer or a crafted persisted document injects arbitrary WordprocessingML (field codes, style refs, extra runs) into a .docx the victim believes they authored. Incomplete fix in the same function the delta touched.

finding.summary: User/peer-controlled `color` and `backgroundColor` strings are interpolated unescaped into DOCX XML attributes, while the sibling `fontFamily` on the same element is explicitly escaped for exactly this reason
finding.evidence: `packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:73` emits `<w:color w:val="${colorHex.replace('#','')}"/>` and :77 `<w:shd ... w:fill="${bgHex.replace('#','')}"/>`; `packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:311` does the same for table-cell background. Only `#` is stripped — no `escapeXmlAttr`, even though the same file defines one at :25 with a comment stating font/style values "originate from untrusted sources (PPTX/DOCX imports, user input in the font picker)". Attack path: (a) victim imports a hostile .docx — `packages/docs/src/import/docx-style-map.ts:62` stores `style.color = '#' + val` with `val` taken verbatim from the attacker's `<w:color w:val=...>`, no format validation; or (b) a collaborator on a shared doc writes an arbitrary `color`/`backgroundColor` Yorkie tree attribute, which `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:177-178` (`parseInlineStyle`) accepts as any string. When the victim then exports to DOCX, a value like `000"/><w:rStyle w:val="x` (or containing `<`/`&`) escapes the attribute and injects arbitrary OOXML into the file the victim downloads/redistributes, at minimum corrupting it and at worst smuggling attacker-chosen run/document markup. This code is pre-existing and outside the diff, but the diff is the color write boundary and its own comment claims to fix what "export paths" see, so the color→export chain is squarely the change's subject matter.

verdict.reason: The finding's central factual claim — that `color`/`backgroundColor` are interpolated into DOCX XML attributes with only `#` stripped and no `escapeXmlAttr` — is false at every location it cites. `packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:78` emits `<w:color w:val="${escapeXmlAttr(colorHex.replace('#', ''))}"/>` and :83 emits `w:fill="${escapeXmlAttr(bgHex.replace('#', ''))}"`; `packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:312` computes `escapeXmlAttr(cell.style.backgroundColor.replace('#', ''))` before interpolating it into `<w:shd ... w:fill>` at :313. The escape helper at docx-style-map.ts:26-33 performs all five canonical XML attribute replacements with `&` first, so a payload such as `000"/><w:rStyle w:val="x` or one containing `<`/`&` is neutralized and cannot break out of the double-quoted attribute. The finding further claims the file's comment covers only `fontFamily`, but the doc comment at :15-25 explicitly names `style.color` and `style.backgroundColor` as untrusted, and :72-75 plus docx-exporter.ts:310-311 carry inline comments giving precisely the import/Yorkie-peer rationale the reviewer says is absent. A repo-wide grep for `replace('#', '')` surfaces only these three XML sinks (all escaped) plus three non-markup contrast/canvas uses (peer-cursor.ts:406, overlay.ts:40, contrast.ts:4) that emit no XML. Both asserted attacker entry points (hostile .docx import, peer-written Yorkie attribute) therefore terminate at escaped sinks, so no OOXML injection is reachable.
